Traditional Christmas Eve Beet Soup

Served at: Christmas Eve

Serves 6Prep 20 minCook 1 hr

Beet soup, often known as borscht, is a vibrant and hearty dish traditionally served on Christmas Eve in many Eastern European households. Its deep red color symbolizes the festive spirit and warmth of the holiday, making it a comforting start to the Christmas feast.

Ingredients

  • 6 medium beets, peeled and grated (about 2 lbs / 900 g)
  • 1 medium onion, finely chopped
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 6 cups (1.4 liters) vegetable broth
  • 2 medium potatoes, peeled and diced
  • 1 large carrot, peeled and grated
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) vegetable oil
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) tomato paste
  • 1 tablespoon (15 ml) lemon juice or vinegar
  • Salt and pepper to taste
  • Fresh dill, chopped, for garnish
  • Sour cream, for serving (optional)

Method

  1. Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat.
  2. Add the chopped onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
  3. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
  4. Stir in the grated beets, grated carrot, and diced potatoes; cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
  5. Add the tomato paste and mix well to coat the vegetables.
  6. Pour in the vegetable broth and bring the mixture to a boil.
  7. Reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered for about 45 minutes, or until the vegetables are tender.
  8. Season with salt, pepper, and lemon juice or vinegar to balance the sweetness of the beets.
  9. Remove from heat and let the soup cool slightly before serving.
  10. Serve hot, garnished with fresh dill and a dollop of sour cream if desired.

Tips

  • For a richer flavor, add a smoked ham bone or smoked sausage during cooking and remove before serving.
  • Use fresh dill for authentic taste; dried dill can be used but add less as it is more concentrated.
  • This soup can be served hot or chilled, depending on your preference and tradition.
